T27 Frobenius / evaluation-place nonconcentration — frozen Phase-IV record v1
2026-10-09

Status: internally derived conditional theorem, independently audited against the source-reported BSSZ function-field construction and T09's selected-place argument. The source construction, curve sequence, and numerical rates remain source-reported; no independent audit of BSSZ's long proof or novelty/priority search is claimed. This record freezes one structural principle and its complete finite-field specialization. It is not a result about arbitrary near-extremizers.

1. Target and theorem

Use Riemann–Roch evaluation at a selected closed point to strengthen the affine-subfield nonconcentration of the BSSZ q=1024 construction past the scalar-action bound. The selected place is chosen by averaging rational-function ratio incidences, not by assuming its evaluation code is generic.

Conditional on BSSZ arXiv:2605.28781v1, Theorem 7.8 and its curve sequence, there is a sequence of prime degrees m_i, curves C_i/F_q, and finite sets B_i⊂F_{q^{m_i}}, q=1024, such that, for all sufficiently large i, writing g_i=g(C_i), n_i=|B_i|, Q_i=q^{m_i},

  m_i/g_i → 85,
  Q_i^0.45 ≤ n_i ≤ Q_i^0.48,
  |B_i+B_i| ≤ n_i^1.89,     |B_iB_i| ≤ n_i^1.91,

and for every proper subfield K⊊F_{q^{m_i}}, every a∈F_{q^{m_i}}, and every ξ∈F_{q^{m_i}}^×,

  |B_i ∩ (a+ξK)| ≤ n_i^{2/3}.                         (1)

The exponents 0.45 and 0.48 are deliberately rounded inward from the source rate interval 0.4594399… to 0.4712561…. The affine-coset exponent 2/3 is also conservative: the incidence exponents below give 0.662958… with an exponential margin. The base subfield F_q has cosets of size at most q=1024, so its fixed scalar orbit is compatible with (1) for large i. In particular this does not assert |B∩(a+ξK)|≤|K|^{1/2} for K=F_q.

Zhelezov, “The sum-product conjecture is false for real numbers,” arXiv:2605.28781v1 (27 May 2026), HTML https://arxiv.org/html/2605.28781v1, §7.3, Theorem 7.8, equations (7.18)–(7.23), states the function-field input used here. T27 Frobenius / evaluation-place nonconcentration — continuation v2
2026-10-09

This continuation records the stronger high-extension-degree consequence of the v1 incidence lemma. It preserves v1 unchanged. Status remains conditional on the BSSZ source construction; all incidence and finite-field deductions below are internally derived.

1. Constant cap by taking m/g→242

Keep q=1024, α=34, β=40.53, ρ_−=39.05239901777024556… and ρ_+=40.05676868555972676… from v1. Choose prime m_i with m_i/g_i→242. This exceeds d_i/g_i→74.53, so degree-m_i evaluation remains injective on L(D_i). The field E_i=F_{q^{m_i}} still has exactly the three proper subfields not contained in F_q:

  K_1=F_{2^{m_i}},  K_2=F_{2^{2m_i}},  K_5=F_{2^{5m_i}}.

The v1 selected-place estimate gives a place v_i with

  Z(v_i) ≤ 12d_i n_i^3 q^{−m_i/2}
        ≤ q^{(3ρ_+−242/2+o(1))g_i}
        = q^{(−0.8296939433…+o(1))g_i} → 0.

Since Z(v_i) is a nonnegative integer, Z(v_i)=0 for large i. If a K_j-affine coset intersects B_i in t points and h=|K_j∩F_q|=2,4,32, then t>h would supply t(t−1)(t−h)>0 nonconstant-ratio incidences, contradicting Z(v_i)=0. Hence

  |B_i∩(a+ξK_j)| ≤ h_j,  h_1=2, h_2=4, h_5=32,

for every a∈E_i and ξ∈E_i^×. For K⊂F_q, a+ξK has at most |K|≤1024 points. Thus the full finite field has the uniform proper-affine-subfield bound

  max_{K⊊E_i} max_{a∈E_i, ξ∈E_i^×} |B_i∩(a+ξK)| ≤ 1024.       (5)

The cardinality rate becomes

  ρ_−/242=0.1613735… ≤ liminf (log_{Q_i}n_i),
  limsup (log_{Q_i}n_i) ≤ ρ_+/242=0.1655238…,

so Q_i^0.16≤n_i≤Q_i^0.17 eventually. The source growth estimates remain |B_i+B_i|≤n_i^1.89 and |B_iB_i|≤n_i^1.91. This is the price of obtaining the fixed cap (5).

2. An orbit transversal meeting the Li–Roche–Newton hypothesis

The construction has F_q^×B_i=B_i. It contains no zero: P_i and G_i consist of nonzero sections, their products are nonzero, and evaluation is injective on L(D_i). The F_q^× action on E_i^× is free, so choose a transversal R_i⊂B_i with exactly one element from each scalar orbit. Then

  |R_i|=n_i/(q−1)=n_i/1023.

For every subfield K⊂F_{q_i}=E_i and every c∈E_i^×:

• If K⊂F_q, then |R_i∩cK|≤1. Indeed, for x,y∈cK, x/y∈K^×⊂F_q^×, so x and y belong to the same F_q^× orbit.
• If K=K_j, then |R_i∩cK_j|≤|B_i∩(0+cK_j)|≤h_j. For all sufficiently large i, h_j≤|K_j|^{1/2}.
• If K=E_i, then |R_i∩cE_i|=|R_i|≤Q_i^{0.17}<Q_i^{1/2}.

T27 Frobenius / evaluation-place nonconcentration — correction v3
2026-10-09

This append-only correction preserves v1 and v2 unchanged.

1. Threshold inequality correction

In v1 §5, the sentence “If t>n_i^{2/3}, then t(t−1)(t−h)>n_i^2 for large i” is too strong as written: for t just above n_i^{2/3}, the two factors (1−1/t)(1−h/t) are below one. The required implication remains valid because the averaged incidence bound is exponentially o(n_i^2). Explicitly, for t≥n_i^{2/3} and fixed h≤32,

  t(t−1)(t−h) ≥ n_i^2 (1−1/t)(1−h/t)
                 = n_i^2(1−o(1)),

whereas (3) and the strict rate gap give Z(v_i)/n_i^2→0. Thus t(t−1)(t−h)>Z(v_i) for large i, contradicting (4). Therefore the stated t≤n_i^{2/3} conclusion is proved.

The same correction applies to the sharper rate statement: from t(t−1)(t−h)≤Z and t>h, one gets t≤max(h, Z^{1/3}(1+o(1))) as t→∞; the exponential estimate then yields every fixed exponent γ>(ρ_+−85/6)/ρ_−.

2. Scalar-action exponent correction

In v1 §5, the elementary scalar-action comparison should use the sumset estimate |B_i+B_i|≤n_i^{1.89}, hence the injection bound is n_i^{1.89/2}=n_i^{0.945}. The printed n_i^{1.91/2}=n_i^{0.955} used the product exponent by mistake. The incidence bound n_i^{2/3} still improves it strictly.
